title: The historical maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona meant that certain personal actions died with the claimant or defendant

content.overview: The historical maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona meant that certain personal actions died with the claimant or defendant. Indian statutes modified that rule, especially through the Fatal Accidents Act 1855 and specialised motor-accident legislation.
content.glance: The historical maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona meant that certain personal actions died with the claimant or defendant. Indian statutes modified that rule, especially through the Fatal Accidents Act 1855 and specialised motor-accident legislation.
content.study: The historical maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona meant that certain personal actions died with the claimant or defendant. Indian statutes modified that rule, especially through the Fatal Accidents Act 1855 and specialised motor-accident legislation.\n\nThe Fatal Accidents Act created a statutory claim for wrongful death by specified relatives. Motor accident claims are governed additionally by the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. Survival of causes belonging to the estate must be distinguished from dependency claims belonging to relatives.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The Fatal Accidents Act created a statutory claim for wrongful death by specified relatives. Motor accident claims are governed additionally by the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. Survival of causes belonging to the estate must be distinguished from dependency claims belonging to relatives.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: The statutory route depends on the nature of the death claim. The Fatal Accidents Act concerns specified dependency-type loss; the Motor Vehicles Act provides a specialised compensation framework. Estate claims must be separately identified.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Identify claimant capacity. 2. Identify statutory cause of action. 3. Prove wrongful act, causation and dependency or estate loss. 4. Avoid double recovery. 5. Apply correct limitation and forum.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Death certificates, medical evidence, income records, dependency proof, succession documents and accident records are central.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Fatal accident claims must use the forum prescribed by the governing statute. Motor accident claims ordinarily proceed before MACT. Check current limitation rules.

distinctions.title: Estate claim vs Dependency claim
distinctions.left: Death in Relation to Tort — Actio Personalis
distinctions.right: An estate claim concerns a cause preserved for the estate; a dependency claim compensates surviving relatives for their own loss.

rows.left: Death-related claims depend on statutory cause of action; an estate claim and a dependency claim must not be conflated.

rows.right: Do not substitute the neighbouring cause of action.
